key_insight: Instead of reusing a fixed class or text embedding at every diffusion step, the paper shows that predicting the next embedding can act as a better condition for image generation. This turns conditioning into a learned sequence prediction problem and can improve how generative models guide denoising.
problem_solved: Diffusion transformers typically rely on a single condition embedding that is reused unchanged across all denoising steps, which may limit expressiveness. The paper asks whether a model can generate more useful conditioning signals by predicting continuous embeddings over time.
method: Introduce Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), a Transformer trained to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
Use the relationship between noisy images, clean images, and their embeddings so that the clean image is treated as the "next" embedding after the noisy-conditioned context.
Replace static conditioning with predicted embeddings during generation to better align the condition with the evolving denoising process.
impact: For AI practitioners, this suggests a new way to condition diffusion models that may be more adaptive and informative than fixed prompts or labels. It could improve image generation quality while opening the door to embedding-prediction-based conditioning for other generative tasks.
